newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen mixed at open, techs seen higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen mixed at open, techs seen higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to have a mixed opening Tuesday, with the recently strong technology sector providing an upward bias.
Bargain-hunters could step in after blue chips finished lower on Monday, analysts said.
Much of the focus will be in the technology stocks, with both Motorola Inc and Advanced Micro Devices Inc due to report second quarter results after the market close.

"Bond prices are off and the futures are up, so it looks like a mixed open," said Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities. "May semiconductor figures were encouraging, so that should put a positive tilt to the chip stocks, which are a very powerful component of the overall market."
The Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was up 0.65 point at 919. The long bond was off 4/32 at a 6.59 percent yield.
Global semiconductor sales rose three percent in May to $11.41 billion, according to the Semiconductor Industry Association's monthly survey.

"The technology sector should continue to do well today," said Thom Brown, managing director of Rutherford Brown and Catherwood. "Motorola, IBM and Hewlett-Packard all look like they're going higher."
On Monday, strength in large-capitalization technology stocks pushed over-the-counter issues to another record high.
The Nasdaq composite gained 3.12 points to close at around 1471. But the Dow Jones Industrial Average finished a choppy session down 37.32 points at 7858.49.
Richard Cripps, chief market strategist at Legg Mason Wood Walker, said stocks could be boosted by bargain-hunting.
"We could see some early morning bargain-hunting in stocks which were down yesterday, like the financials," he said. "I'm looking for a relatively quiet open with an upside bias."
Japan's Nikkei average closed up 148.72 points, or 0.75 percent, at 19,853.89.
In London the FTSE 100 was off 56.9 points at 4753.8. U.S. stocks trading in London were mixed but slightly pressured.
The dollar trimmed its gains against the yen, trading at 112.83/93 yen. In Europe the dollar was steady, trading at 1.7538/52 marks.
The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that some investors believe International Game Technology may be getting serious about a merger with Gtech Holdings Corp.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that Schroder Wertheim & Co has restyled itself as Schroder & Co, but the investment firm plans to remain a niche player.
